target_customer: B2B SaaS sales and marketing teams (first developers needing customer data tooling)
problem: Companies could not see which engaged prospects fit their ideal customer profile; CustomerOS scored them and used AI agents to suggest outreach.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, listed at 2999 dollars per month for the Growth plan

founders.name: Matt Brown
founders.background_notes: Former VP of Product at Voxbone, which Bandwidth acquired in 2020. Source: YC page.

founders.name: Vasi Coscotin
founders.background_notes: About seven years at Voxbone scaling systems and tech teams.

founders.name: Jonty Knox
previous_startups: Otto (fintech, Sequoia Arc first batch in 2022)
founders.background_notes: Crunchbase lists him as co-founder and CPO per a search summary.

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating customer data, scoring ideal-fit and building agents needs data engineering and integrations, standard engineering with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: CRM and marketing platforms like HubSpot could add lead scoring and AI agents, and the repository was open source.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented in the sources read.

market_need_then: The team came from Voxbone and cited their own sales pain. No independent demand evidence was found beyond the company's marketing.

identity.voice_and_tone: Copilot for strategic marketers on the site; the CEO leads with the Voxbone exit story

branding.brand_signature: The Voxbone exit story (about 519M dollars in 2020) used on the site as credibility

rebrands.why: A dead startups archive says the original scope was too narrow; single secondary source

branding.community_and_virality: Open source GitHub repositories under openline-ai and later customeros; no evidence of wider community.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear descriptive name with a distinct domain and a founder credibility story, but generic and no press about the brand itself.

pivots.to: CustomerOS, an open source developer framework for customer data management
pivots.why: Archive says original scope too narrow; single secondary source

pivots.to: AI-agent-based go-to-market and lead intelligence platform

outcome_analysis: The Voxbone alumni team raised a small pre-seed in 2022 after YC Summer 2022 and pivoted at least twice, from Openline to a developer framework and then to an AI go-to-market platform. YC lists it as inactive although the website still shows pricing, and no shutdown report was found, so the cause of any failure is not public.
notes: Funding conflicts: Seedtable shows a single US$500K pre-seed in July 2022 (one database); a dead startups archive says US$2.1M by June 2022 with Cocoa.vc and Crane; Startup-Seeker says US$2.6M. Only the Seedtable round is recorded because the other figures are single unverified sources with no dates. Status conflict: YC says Inactive but customeros.ai is live with pricing, so the exit is unknown. Pivot dates come from the archive only. Competitors left empty because search found only undated or current open source CDP pages.
